\ Isomorphisms in Group Theory

1. The concept of an isomorphism is a fundamental notion in algebra, particularly in group theory, ring theory, and module theory. An isomorphism is a bijective (one-to-one and onto) homomorphism between two algebraic structures of the same type. In the context of group theory, an isomorphism between two groups G and H is a bijective function f: G → H such that f(xy) = f(x)f(y) for all x, y in G. Isomorphisms satisfy several important properties, such as preserving the group operation and subgroup structure. Isomorphic groups are considered to be "the same" in terms of their group structure, even if their underlying sets are different.
